newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Ballarat Brewing opposes GPG BID.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Ballarat Brewing opposes GPG BID.

text.p: Ballarat Brewing Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it strenuously opposed the application by Guinness Peat Group to make a full takeover bid for the company.
GPG said on Monday it had sought approval from the Australian Securities Commission to alter its bid, which had previously been a proportional offer.

"Ballarat Brewing strenuously opposes GPG's application on the basis that GPG's takeover scheme is no longer of any practical effect, due to the overwhelming rejection of that scheme by Ballarat Brewing shareholders at the extraordinary general meeting held on 12 August, 1996," the company said.
"Ballarat Brewing also considers that a "conversion" of GPS's takeover scheme in the manner suggested would be contrary to law and contrary to the interests of shareholders."

While Ballarat Brewing said its opposition would be forwarded to the ASC by its lawyers, the company also said it would not object to any new bid from GPG for all the shares held by Ballarat Brewing shareholders. The GPG bid was based on the purchase of 50 percent of each investor's shares.
Ballarat said any new bid from GPG for all shares should be made in a manner which complies with the law and which does not add to the confusion arising out of its actions to date.
"This would require the preparation of a new Part A statement and offer document complying with the law."

GPG's current partial offer of A$2.45 is due to close on October 8. Ballarat Brewing, a tourism and leisure group which once had brewing links, had told its shareholders to take no action in relation to the bid.
Foster's Brewing Group Ltd is the largest investor in Ballarat Brewing with a 33 percent stake and has said a rival bid or other response could not be ruled out.
Ballarat Brewing shares last traded at A$2.50 on Friday.
